note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape (grouped wizard form; the grader flattens it). `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`.

personas.name: final-no-abnormality
personas.description: Complete final clinic-review reply: normal examination and echo, non-cardiac musculoskeletal cause, discharged back to the GP — expect no-abnormality, severity none, full completeness, routine follow-up.

assessment.clinicalSummary: Reviewed in clinic for atypical chest discomfort. History suggests a musculoskeletal origin; reproducible on palpation.
assessment.examinationFindings: Heart sounds normal, no murmurs, chest wall tenderness over costochondral junctions. BP 128/78.
assessment.investigationsPerformed: Resting ECG normal. Transthoracic echo: structurally normal heart, EF 62%.

diagnosis.diagnosisNarrative: Costochondritis; no evidence of cardiac disease.

management.managementPlan: Reassurance given. Simple analgesia as needed. No cardiology follow-up required.
management.recommendedFollowUp: Discharge to GP; re-refer if symptoms change character.

expected.recommendedAction: No specific cardiology follow-up required; discharge back to the referrer for usual care.

firedRules.description: No structured cardiac finding and a non-cardiac / no-abnormality conclusion; classified as no abnormality.
No structured cardiac finding; condition severity graded none.
No escalation rule fired; routine follow-up only.

personas.name: heart-failure-reduced-ef
personas.description: Final reply diagnosing heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 32%): full sections, medication changes started, urgent HF-nurse follow-up — expect cardiac-condition, major severity, urgent follow-up.

assessment.clinicalSummary: Progressive exertional breathlessness and ankle swelling over three months; NYHA class III at review.
assessment.examinationFindings: Raised JVP, bibasal crackles, mild pitting oedema to mid-shin. BP 142/88, HR 92 regular.
assessment.investigationsPerformed: NT-proBNP 2,340 ng/L. Echo: dilated LV, global hypokinesia, EF 32%. ECG: LBBB.

diagnosis.diagnosisNarrative: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, likely non-ischaemic; awaiting angiography to exclude CAD.

management.managementPlan: Start four-pillar HF therapy; daily weights; refer to HF specialist nurse; outpatient angiogram requested.
management.medicationChanges: Started ramipril 2.5 mg od, bisoprolol 1.25 mg od, dapagliflozin 10 mg od, spironolactone 25 mg od.
management.recommendedFollowUp: HF nurse review in 2 weeks with bloods; clinic review in 6 weeks with repeat echo at 3 months.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange urgent cardiology follow-up and expedite specialist management as clinically indicated.

firedRules.description: One or more structured cardiac findings or a cardiac diagnosis are present; classified as a cardiac condition.
Reduced left-ventricular ejection fraction (HFrEF); condition severity graded major.
Major cardiac condition present; follow-up urgency graded urgent.

flags.description: Reduced left-ventricular ejection fraction (heart failure with reduced ejection fraction).
flags.suggestedAction: Start / optimise guideline-directed heart-failure therapy and arrange heart-failure service follow-up per NICE NG106.

personas.name: critical-uncommunicated-preliminary
personas.description: Preliminary inpatient reply with a critical finding (severe aortic stenosis with syncope) marked critical but NOT yet communicated, management sections still empty — expect critical classification, critical-alert follow-up, and the uncommunicated-critical-result / incompleteness rules to fire.

assessment.clinicalSummary: Seen on the ward after exertional syncope. Loud ejection systolic murmur radiating to carotids.
assessment.investigationsPerformed: Bedside echo: heavily calcified aortic valve, peak gradient 82 mmHg, AVA 0.7 cm2.

expected.recommendedAction: Communicate the critical result directly to the referrer now and arrange urgent review; document the conversation.

firedRules.description: A critical or unexpected significant cardiac result is present; classified as critical.
Critical result present; condition severity graded major.
Mandatory response section missing: management plan.
Mandatory response section missing: recommended follow-up.
Critical result auto-escalates follow-up urgency to critical-alert regardless of the other axes.

flags.description: A critical or unexpected significant cardiac result is present (e.g. critical arrhythmia, severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, acute coronary syndrome).
flags.suggestedAction: Communicate the critical result to the referrer immediately, arrange urgent review, and document the communication.

flags.description: Critical result present but it has not been recorded as communicated to the referrer.
flags.suggestedAction: Contact the referrer now and record who was informed, with date and time.

flags.description: Significant (moderate–severe) valve disease requiring specialist management.
flags.suggestedAction: Refer to the valve / structural heart team and consider Heart Team discussion per ESC/EACTS guidance.

flags.description: One or more mandatory response sections are missing (2 of summary / examination / management / follow-up).
flags.suggestedAction: Complete the missing response sections before finalising the reply.
